alignments.note: Ordinary prohibitive μή with the present imperative, aligned to *not*. Rule 44 does not apply: the particle marks a prohibition, not a question. Rules 41 and 59 do not apply either, since no negative indefinite follows for the negation to be written into, so the negator keeps its own English word.

Present passive imperative rendered by the periphrastic *Be ... deceived*; the copular auxiliary is the verb's own inflection-licensed helper under rule 9, and rule 17 heads on the lexical participle *deceived* rather than on the auxiliary. Discontinuous across *not* under rule 15. Not merged with μή: the ASV writes a separate word for each token, so rule 2 splits them and rule 39's single-word test is not met.

Anarthrous vocative taking *brethren* alone. Rule 89 is not engaged in either arm: no article stands to take an address word, and the ASV supplies no *ye* or *O* for the noun to carry as a rule 7 helper.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *my*. Rule 20's displacement question does not arise: the Greek phrase is anarthrous, so there is no article for the possessive to empty.

Attributive adjective on its own English word, split from its noun under rules 2 and 26. Rule 58 is not engaged: no determiner is supplied for the phrase — the only prenominal word is the possessive *my*, which belongs to μου — so adjective and noun each stand alone.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned unchanged in substance. All five source and six target ids are partitioned exactly once; every source token has a distinct English realization, so there are no unrepresented, added or noncompositional units.

Heads audited separately from edges under rule 28. The only live head question is πλανᾶσθε, where rule 17 requires the lexical *deceived* over the auxiliary *Be*; the other four units are one-token-to-one-token and take their sole tokens under rule 10.

Word order differs (Greek ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί against ASV *my beloved brethren*). Rule 15 permits the reordering and rule 26 forbids bundling a transparent noun phrase, so the three tokens stay three units rather than one reordered block.
Notes rewritten only for precision: the s005 note previously wrote the lemma as "μou" with a Latin o, and the s003 note now rules out both arms of rule 89 rather than one.
